about: Radio and intercom for chapter 8: the rendezvous and docking in lunar orbit, and the way up through the tunnel. Time lines lead up to the docking at GET 187:37:15; the docking, the opening of the tunnel, setting off up it and sitting down in the Command Module are cued by what happens. t = GET (seconds from liftoff). Original lines in the style of the Apollo air-to-ground; not quotes.

lines.text: Challenger, Houston. Your orbit is good. America is two hundred and twenty kilometres ahead of you.
There she is. That bright star, dead ahead. Run the clock on, and we'll catch her.
Challenger, America. I have you on the sextant. You are a little light down there against the Moon.
Braking. Thirty feet a second, coming down nicely.
Challenger, America. I can see your thrusters firing. You look beautiful.
Look at that. America, right outside the window.
Hold her there, Challenger. I am coming round over the top to dock.
Challenger, America, Houston. You are go for docking.
Capture! And the latches. Hard dock.
Roger, we copy hard dock. Welcome back, Challenger.
The hatch is out. Come on up, and bring those rocks with you.
Go ahead. I'll pass the sample boxes up behind you.
Welcome home. You look like a couple of coal miners.
America, Houston. Three men and a hundred kilos of Moon, all in one ship. Nice work.
